phases.name: Authenticate and accept a wire command
phases.description: Define the authenticated API boundary and one durable idempotency identity per transfer intent.

phases.name: Verify ownership, policy, and real-time risk
phases.description: Check account ownership, limits, KYC/AML, sanctions, and fraud before allowing rail dispatch.

phases.name: Commit and dispatch domestic and international wires
phases.description: Atomically record the intent and outbox, then dispatch through idempotent rail adapters and expose honest status.

phases.name: Track outcomes, audit, and recover
phases.description: Reconcile uncertain rail results, archive audit evidence, and protect the no-loss path with monitoring and managed keys.

steps.phase: Authenticate and accept a wire command
steps.title: Read the frozen wire-transfer brief
steps.content: The frozen brief requires domestic and international initiation, account verification, transaction limits, fraud prevention, AML/KYC, status tracking, idempotent API calls, and an audit trail. Its constraints are ACID guarantees, high security and encryption, regulatory compliance, real-time fraud detection, and zero tolerance for data loss. It gives no throughput, latency target, jurisdictions, rail contracts, currencies, retention term, or recovery target. Treat those as decisions requiring bank and compliance-owner approval, not as promises supplied by the brief. An accepted request is not a settled wire.

steps.phase: Authenticate and accept a wire command
steps.title: Add the bank client
steps.content: The authorized customer or bank operator submits a wire instruction with a stable idempotency key and reads status by the returned transfer ID. The client does not decide whether a wire has settled.

component.label: Bank Client
component.description: Authorized transfer initiation and status reads

properties.purpose: Submit domestic or international wire instructions with a stable idempotency key; display pending, review, failed, and confirmed states from the server, never infer settlement from a timeout.

component.highlightReason: The existing Web App component represents the customer or operator entry point.

steps.phase: Authenticate and accept a wire command
steps.title: Add the protected API boundary
steps.content: Validate the instruction shape, authenticate each request, enforce transport encryption and quotas, and pass a request correlation ID. Neither the gateway nor an in-memory cache is the idempotency authority.

component.label: Wire API Gateway

properties.purpose: Require TLS, validate request shape and authorization context, bound request rates, reject raw secrets in logs, and route initiation and status requests with a correlation ID.

component.highlightReason: The existing API Gateway is the entry and policy enforcement point.

steps.phase: Authenticate and accept a wire command
steps.title: Route initiate and status calls
steps.content: POST /wires includes the same idempotency key on retries. GET /wires/{id} is authorized to the owning principal and returns a server-side state, including an explicit unknown or pending outcome.

connection.label: Initiate + status over TLS
connection.description: Authenticated calls carry a stable idempotency key and correlation ID

steps.phase: Authenticate and accept a wire command
steps.title: Add identity and step-up authentication
steps.content: Verify the principal and permitted account scope. Require step-up MFA for the bank-approved high-risk or high-value policy; MFA does not replace transaction authorization or KYC.

component.label: Identity + MFA
component.description: Principal, account scope, and step-up proof

properties.purpose: Issue and verify short-lived principal and account-scope claims, require policy-triggered MFA, and record actor and step-up proof without storing credentials in wire events.

component.highlightReason: The existing Auth Service matches identity and MFA controls.

steps.phase: Authenticate and accept a wire command
steps.title: Validate identity on every command
steps.content: The gateway verifies identity, token audience, account scope, and step-up claims for initiation. A status read has its own authorization check; possession of a transfer ID is insufficient.

connection.label: Identity + MFA decision
connection.description: Validate principal, account scope, and policy-required step-up

steps.phase: Authenticate and accept a wire command
steps.title: Add the wire command and status service
steps.content: Normalize beneficiary, amount, currency, destination country, and domestic or international route. Reject conflicting reuses of an idempotency key. Do not respond with SETTLED until a verified rail outcome is committed.

component.label: Wire Command + Status Service

properties.purpose: Validate domestic and international instructions; bind principal, source account, beneficiary, amount, currency and payload hash to a scoped idempotency key; call all pre-dispatch gates; commit an intent or durable rejection; return a transfer ID and truthful status. GET status reads the authoritative ledger with account authorization.

component.highlightReason: The existing Backend Server is the application command and query boundary.

steps.phase: Authenticate and accept a wire command
steps.title: Forward validated requests
steps.content: Only a validated identity context and typed wire instruction reach the command service. The service rechecks resource authorization and never trusts a client-supplied status.

connection.label: Authorized wire command + status
connection.description: Forward account-scoped initiation and read requests with correlation ID

steps.phase: Authenticate and accept a wire command
steps.title: Choose durable idempotency semantics
steps.content: Scope the idempotency key to principal and operation, hash the full normalized instruction, and reserve it under a unique constraint in the same ACID transaction as the intent. Concurrent identical requests return the same transfer ID and state; a reused key with a different payload conflicts. A timeout is resolved by key lookup before a new attempt.

decision.question: Where is duplicate transfer prevention enforced?
decision.chosen: Durable unique idempotency record and wire intent in one ledger transaction
decision.chosenReason: A process crash, retry, or concurrent request cannot turn one logical instruction into two dispatchable wires.

alternatives.tradeoff: Expiry, failover, and concurrency can allow a second money movement.
Turns a lost response into a duplicate transfer.

properties.purpose: Validate domestic and international instructions; bind principal, source account, beneficiary, amount, currency and payload hash to a scoped idempotency key; resolve concurrent retries through the ledger's unique record; call all pre-dispatch gates; commit an intent or durable rejection; return a transfer ID and truthful status. GET status reads the authoritative ledger with account authorization.

steps.phase: Verify ownership, policy, and real-time risk
steps.title: Add the authoritative ACID ledger
steps.content: Use a relational OLTP ledger for accounts, transfer intents, idempotency records, funds holds/postings, versioned status, decision references, and an outbox. Transactional invariants balance entries per currency; immutable corrections are new reversal entries, never edits to posted history.

component.label: ACID Wire Ledger + Outbox
component.description: Accounts, intents, postings, statuses, and durable outbox

properties.purpose: Authoritative ACID account and transfer state: unique scoped idempotency key plus payload hash, atomic limit/funds reservation, balanced immutable postings, monotonic status versions, denied-attempt evidence, policy and risk references, and transactional outbox. Acknowledgement follows durable commit; no rail success is invented from dispatch alone.

component.highlightReason: The existing Database component can model a transactional relational ledger without a custom node.

steps.phase: Verify ownership, policy, and real-time risk
steps.title: Add account and beneficiary verification
steps.content: Check source-account ownership, active/unfrozen state, sufficient available funds, and beneficiary/routing details. External beneficiary-bank ownership cannot be assumed verified merely because a format check passed.

component.label: Account Verification

properties.purpose: Check principal-to-source-account ownership, account status and available funds from authoritative records; validate beneficiary and routing fields for the selected domestic or international rail; distinguish format validation from external account ownership confirmation.

component.highlightReason: The existing Backend Server represents account verification logic.

steps.phase: Verify ownership, policy, and real-time risk
steps.title: Invoke account checks before dispatch
steps.content: The command service passes authenticated source account and beneficiary data to verification before a dispatchable intent is committed.

connection.label: Verify account + beneficiary
connection.description: Reject unowned, frozen, insufficient, or malformed accounts before rail dispatch

steps.phase: Verify ownership, policy, and real-time risk
steps.title: Read authoritative account state
steps.content: Read versioned account state from the ledger. Recheck balance and hold conditions inside the final transaction so concurrent wires cannot race on a stale preflight read.

connection.label: Owner, status + funds
connection.description: Preflight account state; final funds reservation is checked atomically at commit

steps.phase: Verify ownership, policy, and real-time risk
steps.title: Add transaction limits and controls
steps.content: Apply bank-configured per-transfer, daily, velocity, corridor, and role limits. A precheck improves feedback, but the final counter and funds reservation must be atomic with the wire intent.

component.label: Limits + Controls

properties.purpose: Evaluate bank-approved amount, daily aggregate, velocity, corridor and role controls; expose the policy version and denial reason. Reserve limits and funds with the intent in one ACID transaction so concurrent wires cannot exceed controls.

component.highlightReason: A Backend Server can express policy checks without inventing a limit-service catalog type.

steps.phase: Verify ownership, policy, and real-time risk
steps.title: Gate the command on limits
steps.content: Run controls before dispatch. A limit failure is a durable rejection with an audit reference, not an accepted wire awaiting settlement.

connection.label: Limit decision
connection.description: Apply amount, daily, velocity, and corridor controls to the normalized instruction

steps.phase: Verify ownership, policy, and real-time risk
steps.title: Use committed counters for concurrency
steps.content: Read prior activity and pass a versioned limit decision to the ledger. The final transaction conditionally reserves the limit bucket and source funds; retrying the same intent does not reserve twice.

connection.label: Versioned limit state
connection.description: Atomic final reservation prevents concurrent wires from bypassing aggregate limits

steps.phase: Verify ownership, policy, and real-time risk
steps.title: Add compliance screening
steps.content: Apply jurisdiction-approved KYC, AML and sanctions rules to originator, beneficiary, corridor, and transaction context. A possible match enters review; a prohibited match blocks dispatch. Rules, retention, and escalation paths need compliance-owner signoff.

component.label: KYC + AML Screening

properties.purpose: Apply approved jurisdiction-specific KYC, AML, sanctions, and corridor rules before dispatch; produce allow, reject, or manual-review with policy version, reason codes, and evidence reference. Fail closed or hold when required data or screening is unavailable.

component.highlightReason: The existing Backend Server supports this policy and review role.

steps.phase: Verify ownership, policy, and real-time risk
steps.title: Screen before a dispatchable intent
steps.content: Pass a minimized originator and beneficiary context for screening. Do not route a held or prohibited wire to a bank rail.

connection.label: AML, KYC + sanctions decision
connection.description: Block or hold based on versioned compliance policy before rail dispatch

steps.phase: Verify ownership, policy, and real-time risk
steps.title: Add restricted KYC evidence
steps.content: Separate sensitive identity evidence from routine wire records. Grant least-privilege access, encrypt it, and apply jurisdiction-approved retention and legal hold rules rather than an invented global period.

component.label: Restricted KYC Records

properties.purpose: Store encrypted, access-audited customer identity evidence and screening references with jurisdiction-approved retention and legal holds; expose only minimum necessary attributes to screening, not raw documents to rail dispatch.

component.highlightReason: The existing Database component can represent a restricted evidence store.

steps.phase: Verify ownership, policy, and real-time risk
steps.title: Read approved identity evidence
steps.content: The compliance service requests only current verified identity and screening facts, recording evidence and rule versions for review.

connection.label: Minimal KYC facts
connection.description: Least-privilege evidence lookup with policy and access audit

steps.phase: Verify ownership, policy, and real-time risk
steps.title: Compare against transaction history
steps.content: Use prior committed transfer history for AML velocity and pattern checks. Keep the evidence reference and policy version, but do not copy full KYC documents into the ledger.

connection.label: AML history lookup
connection.description: Risk-minimized transaction history and versioned decision reference

steps.phase: Verify ownership, policy, and real-time risk
steps.title: Add the synchronous fraud gate
steps.content: Score the wire before it can be dispatched, using account history, velocity, beneficiary novelty and approved device/context signals. Return allow, review, or reject with reasons and feature age; the model cannot post money.

component.label: Real-time Fraud Gate

properties.purpose: Synchronously combine deterministic rules and a versioned fraud model before dispatch; return allow, manual-review, or reject with reason codes, model and feature versions. Missing or stale risk evidence holds the wire rather than silently approving it.

component.highlightReason: The existing Backend Server models risk-policy orchestration.

steps.phase: Verify ownership, policy, and real-time risk
steps.title: Require fraud screening before dispatch
steps.content: The command service waits for the real-time decision or records REVIEW if the bounded fraud call is unavailable. It never treats a timeout as an approval.

connection.label: Pre-dispatch fraud decision
connection.description: Allow, review, or reject before a dispatchable ledger state exists

steps.phase: Verify ownership, policy, and real-time risk
steps.title: Add a versioned fraud model serving endpoint
steps.content: The model supplies a score and reason codes from approved minimized features. Rules and review remain the policy authority, especially during model outage or drift.

component.label: Fraud Model Serving

properties.purpose: Serve a versioned fraud score with reason codes and feature freshness for a pre-dispatch decision; never write balances or independently approve a regulated transfer.

component.highlightReason: Model Serving is an existing catalog component for online inference.

steps.phase: Verify ownership, policy, and real-time risk
steps.title: Request a bounded risk score
steps.content: Record model version, feature timestamp, score, and decision reference. A model error routes to review or rejection under policy; it never implicitly becomes allow.

connection.label: Versioned fraud score
connection.description: Bounded real-time inference with model and feature provenance

steps.phase: Verify ownership, policy, and real-time risk
steps.title: Use history for fraud velocity
steps.content: Read committed account and beneficiary history for velocity and novelty features. The ledger remains the source of truth; a cache cannot authorize a wire against stale funds or limits.

connection.label: Fraud history + velocity
connection.description: Versioned committed history supports pre-dispatch fraud checks

steps.phase: Commit and dispatch domestic and international wires
steps.title: Choose a fail-closed pre-dispatch policy
steps.content: No dispatchable intent exists until ownership, limits, compliance, and fraud decisions are complete. Unknown or ambiguous outcomes become a durable REVIEW or PENDING state with a case reference. A reviewer may release only under an approved, audited procedure.

decision.question: What happens when screening is unavailable or inconclusive?
decision.chosen: Hold the wire for reviewed resolution and block rail dispatch
decision.chosenReason: Automatic approval would violate the real-time fraud and regulatory gates; a durable hold preserves an honest status and evidence trail.

alternatives.option: Fail open and send the wire
alternatives.tradeoff: Can move funds without required fraud or compliance clearance.

alternatives.option: Drop the request without a record
alternatives.tradeoff: Loses audit and status evidence for an attempted transaction.

properties.purpose: Synchronously combine deterministic rules and a versioned fraud model before dispatch; return allow, manual-review, or reject with reason codes, model and feature versions. Missing, stale, or inconclusive risk evidence creates a durable hold and blocks the rail until approved review resolves it.

steps.phase: Commit and dispatch domestic and international wires
steps.title: Commit one intent and its evidence
steps.content: In one ACID transaction, conditionally reserve the idempotency key, recheck funds and limits, store the wire intent and state, append audit and outbox records, then commit before acknowledging. A denied attempt also gets a durable audit outcome; if durable commit fails, return a retryable error without claiming acceptance.

connection.label: ACID intent + idempotency + outbox
connection.description: Atomic reservation, state, audit reference, and dispatch outbox before acknowledgement

steps.phase: Commit and dispatch domestic and international wires
steps.title: Choose local ACID and durable outbox boundaries
steps.content: The bank rail cannot participate in the ledger transaction. Commit the local intent, hold/posting, status, and dispatch event atomically; relay after commit. A failed or reversed external leg needs a new compensating ledger entry and reconciliation, never editing posted history or claiming cross-system ACID.

decision.question: How are a local ACID commit and an external rail operation coordinated?
decision.chosen: Transactional outbox plus idempotent dispatch, reconciliation, and compensating entries
decision.chosenReason: It closes the crash gap between ledger commit and publish while acknowledging that the external rail is outside the database transaction.

alternatives.option: Write the rail first, then the ledger
alternatives.tradeoff: A crash can move funds without a local authoritative record.

alternatives.option: Assume one distributed ACID transaction across all banks
alternatives.tradeoff: External clearing rails do not provide that atomic boundary.

steps.phase: Commit and dispatch domestic and international wires
steps.title: Add the committed-outbox relay
steps.content: Poll committed outbox rows and publish at least once. Mark publication progress only after durable queue acceptance; restart or replay uses the same event ID.

component.label: Outbox Relay

properties.purpose: Read committed ledger outbox rows, publish stable event IDs at least once, checkpoint only after durable queue or archive acknowledgement, and retry without losing or duplicating a logical transfer.

component.highlightReason: The existing Processing Worker supports a replayable relay.

steps.phase: Commit and dispatch domestic and international wires
steps.title: Read only committed outbox events
steps.content: The relay never publishes a rolled-back transfer. A crash after queue publish but before marking the outbox complete produces a duplicate event ID, which consumers deduplicate.

connection.label: Committed outbox events
connection.description: Stable IDs permit replay after a crash without losing an accepted wire

steps.phase: Commit and dispatch domestic and international wires
steps.title: Add a durable dispatch queue
steps.content: Buffer rail work after the ACID commit. Preserve transfer ID, version, route, and event ID; alert on oldest-message age and dead letters. Queue delivery can repeat, so the dispatcher must be idempotent.

component.label: Durable Rail Dispatch Queue

properties.purpose: Hold committed, approved wire dispatch events with transfer ID, state version and stable event ID; absorb bursts and rail outages; retain retry and dead-letter evidence. Never mistake enqueue for settlement.

component.highlightReason: The existing Queue represents durable asynchronous dispatch.

steps.phase: Commit and dispatch domestic and international wires
steps.title: Publish without a commit-to-queue gap
steps.content: Publish the committed outbox event and acknowledge only after durable queue receipt. On failure the outbox remains pending for replay; on duplicate receipt the event ID identifies the same transfer.

connection.label: Approved wire event
connection.description: At-least-once publish with stable event ID and bounded backpressure

steps.phase: Commit and dispatch domestic and international wires
steps.title: Add idempotent rail dispatch
steps.content: Consume only approved transfer versions. Persist a stable rail operation ID before external submission. On timeout, query by that reference or reconcile; never send a new payment merely because the response was lost.

component.label: Rail Dispatch Worker

properties.purpose: Route approved domestic and international wires with stable per-transfer rail operation IDs, deduplicate queue events, verify signed rail callbacks, persist monotonic outcomes, and reconcile ambiguous timeouts before any replay. Never blindly resubmit a money movement.

component.highlightReason: The existing Processing Worker fits queued and retryable rail dispatch.

steps.phase: Commit and dispatch domestic and international wires
steps.title: Consume approved committed work
steps.content: The dispatcher checks current ledger version before submitting. Duplicate or stale queue deliveries are no-ops; a held or reversed wire cannot be sent by an old message.

connection.label: Approved transfer command
connection.description: Deduplicate by transfer ID and state version before any rail call

steps.phase: Commit and dispatch domestic and international wires
steps.title: Add the domestic clearing adapter
steps.content: The domestic adapter validates local routing and rail-specific limits, transmits a stable instruction reference, and returns an accepted or confirmed outcome according to the actual rail contract.

component.label: Domestic Rail Adapter

properties.purpose: Submit domestic wires through a bank-approved clearing integration with a stable operation reference; distinguish accepted, pending, rejected and confirmed settlement outcomes. Rail protocol and deadlines require bank approval.

component.highlightReason: The existing Payment Service can represent a bank-rail integration without a custom component.

steps.phase: Commit and dispatch domestic and international wires
steps.title: Submit domestic instructions
steps.content: Send only approved domestic wires with the persisted operation reference. Retry only when the rail contract guarantees idempotent lookup or submission by that same reference.

connection.label: Domestic wire submission
connection.description: Stable rail reference and contract-specific retry semantics

steps.phase: Commit and dispatch domestic and international wires
steps.title: Add the international rail adapter
steps.content: Validate beneficiary bank identifiers, destination country, currency, sanctions context and any required FX quote before a dispatchable intent is committed. The adapter rechecks rail-specific fields and preserves the accepted quote and fees if conversion applies; no particular corridor or rail is mandated by the brief.

component.label: International Rail Adapter

properties.purpose: Submit approved cross-border wires through bank-approved correspondent or network integration; validate beneficiary and country/currency routing, bind any required FX quote and fees, reuse stable operation references, and distinguish pending from confirmed settlement.

component.highlightReason: The existing Payment Service also covers an international bank-rail adapter.

steps.phase: Commit and dispatch domestic and international wires
steps.title: Submit cross-border instructions
steps.content: Send the approved international instruction with preserved quote, fees, beneficiary context, and stable operation reference. A correspondent acknowledgement is not final settlement.

connection.label: International wire submission
connection.description: Approved corridor and stable reference; pending until confirmed outcome

steps.phase: Commit and dispatch domestic and international wires
steps.title: Ingest domestic rail outcomes
steps.content: Authenticate rail callbacks or signed reports, deduplicate by provider event ID, and retain the raw reference for reconciliation. Delayed or reordered outcomes cannot regress a terminal state.

connection.label: Domestic outcome
connection.description: Verified callback or report with operation ID and monotonic state transition

steps.phase: Commit and dispatch domestic and international wires
steps.title: Ingest international rail outcomes
steps.content: Treat correspondent acknowledgements as PENDING unless the actual contract confirms settlement. Preserve country, currency, provider reference, and event sequence for compliance and repair.

connection.label: International outcome
connection.description: Verified, deduplicated callback or settlement report with finality semantics

steps.phase: Commit and dispatch domestic and international wires
steps.title: Commit rail outcomes and new audit events
steps.content: Atomically advance the transfer state by version, post final or compensating ledger entries, record a signed-outcome reference, and append a status/audit outbox event. Never overwrite immutable postings or mark an unknown rail outcome as failed and safely retryable.

connection.label: Versioned rail outcome + posting
connection.description: ACID state transition, immutable ledger entry, and audit outbox

steps.phase: Commit and dispatch domestic and international wires
steps.title: Scale on backlog without duplicate money movement
steps.content: Scale dispatch workers only when durable queue age and rail capacity justify it. Partition or lease by transfer ID and keep ledger-version checks so competing workers cannot dispatch the same operation twice. Backpressure leaves accepted wires durably pending, never silently dropped.

scaleTrigger.metric: Oldest approved dispatch event age and rail error/timeout rate
scaleTrigger.action: Add bounded workers per rail while preserving stable operation IDs, per-transfer leases, and provider quotas
scaleTrigger.impact: Absorbs bursts and isolates slow rails; finality still depends on rail confirmation and reconciliation.

steps.phase: Commit and dispatch domestic and international wires
steps.title: Read authoritative transfer status
steps.content: GET status returns versioned RECEIVED, REVIEW, PENDING_RAIL, SETTLED, FAILED, or REVERSED states as appropriate. A timeout or missing callback remains PENDING/UNKNOWN until reconciled. Enforce owner and support-role authorization on every read.

connection.label: Authorized status lookup
connection.description: Read durable state, finality evidence, and version by transfer ID

steps.phase: Track outcomes, audit, and recover
steps.title: Add rail reconciliation
steps.content: Compare provider reports and queryable rail references to ledger states. Repair missing, duplicate, delayed, or mismatched outcomes by reviewed compensating entries; do not blindly resend on an ambiguous timeout.

component.label: Rail Reconciliation

properties.purpose: Match signed domestic/international settlement reports and stable operation references against ledger postings; surface unknown, duplicate, delayed and amount/currency mismatches; open auditable repair cases and post approved compensating entries instead of erasing history or blind resubmission.

component.highlightReason: The existing Processing Worker can model repeatable reconciliation jobs.

steps.phase: Track outcomes, audit, and recover
steps.title: Supply references for reconciliation
steps.content: Pass each submitted operation reference and last known provider outcome to reconciliation. The worker can independently query or ingest the actual rail's signed report.

connection.label: Submitted rail references
connection.description: Track ambiguous timeouts and delayed settlement evidence

steps.phase: Track outcomes, audit, and recover
steps.title: Reconcile against immutable ledger state
steps.content: Match by transfer and rail operation IDs, amounts, currency, and state version. Escalate gaps before retry or reversal. A repair is a new audited transition with an outbox event.

connection.label: Match, investigate + compensate
connection.description: Detect discrepancies and append reviewed, versioned corrective entries

steps.phase: Track outcomes, audit, and recover
steps.title: Add protected audit evidence archive
steps.content: Archive immutable, integrity-checked event envelopes for every attempted transaction, status change, screening decision, privileged review, and repair. Exclude secrets and unnecessary identity documents; apply approved residency, retention, legal hold and access review by jurisdiction.

component.label: Protected Audit Archive

properties.purpose: Retain encrypted, integrity-checked and access-audited envelopes for initiations, denials, AML/KYC and fraud decisions, rail outcomes, status versions, reviewer actions and repairs. Apply compliance-approved jurisdictional retention, residency and legal holds; never archive credentials or full KYC documents in routine wire events.

component.highlightReason: Cold Storage is the existing catalog role for long-lived protected audit evidence.

steps.phase: Track outcomes, audit, and recover
steps.title: Export committed audit events
steps.content: The outbox relay publishes privacy-minimized, hash-linked audit envelopes after commit. Archive acknowledgement is tracked separately from queue publish so a failed archive write remains retryable and visible.

connection.label: Committed audit envelope
connection.description: Retry until archive acknowledgement; preserve event ID and hash chain

steps.phase: Track outcomes, audit, and recover
steps.title: Add financial and operational monitoring
steps.content: Alert on ledger imbalance, missing outbox or archive acknowledgements, queue age, stuck review/pending wires, rail timeouts, fraud fallback, reconciliation gaps, and restore failures. Avoid sensitive payloads in metrics.

component.label: Wire Invariant Monitoring

properties.purpose: Alert on unbalanced postings, failed ACID commits, outbox and archive lag, oldest queue age, stuck PENDING/REVIEW wires, fraud-screening outage, rail ambiguity, reconciliation mismatches, backup and restore verification; never log raw KYC data or secrets.

component.highlightReason: The existing Monitoring component exposes financial invariants and recovery signals.

steps.phase: Track outcomes, audit, and recover
steps.title: Alert on ledger and outbox invariants
steps.content: Any missing committed event, out-of-balance posting, broken backup/restore check, or unacknowledged audit export opens an incident. Multi-AZ replication, WAL, PITR and tested restoration reduce loss risk but need measured recovery evidence.

connection.label: Ledger + outbox invariants
connection.description: Detect imbalance, stuck states, audit lag, and restore failures

steps.phase: Track outcomes, audit, and recover
steps.title: Alert on durable dispatch lag
steps.content: Measure oldest-message age, retry rate, dead letters, and per-rail backpressure. Pause unsafe dispatch and reconcile before redrive; redrive retains the same transfer and rail operation IDs.

connection.label: Queue age + retry signals
connection.description: Detect unprocessed accepted wires and unsafe replay before data loss

steps.phase: Track outcomes, audit, and recover
steps.title: Add managed secrets and encryption keys
steps.content: Use managed keys for encrypted ledger, KYC and audit data, and short-lived credentials for gateway and rail adapters. Rotate keys with audit and dual control; never place credentials in wire payloads, event buses or logs.

component.label: Keys + Secrets Manager

properties.purpose: Manage and rotate encryption keys and scoped rail/API credentials with audited least-privilege access; support TLS and encrypted ledger, KYC and audit evidence without exposing secrets to events or logs.

component.highlightReason: The existing Secrets Manager fits key and credential lifecycle control.

steps.phase: Track outcomes, audit, and recover
steps.title: Protect gateway credentials
steps.content: The gateway retrieves scoped authentication and TLS material through managed access; rotate and audit privileged reads.

connection.label: TLS + authentication secrets
connection.description: Short-lived scoped credentials with rotation and access audit

steps.phase: Track outcomes, audit, and recover
steps.title: Protect financial records
steps.content: Encrypt ledger storage and backups, separate key administration from wire operations, and audit decrypt privileges. Key access failure fails closed for new money movement.

connection.label: Ledger encryption keys
connection.description: Managed key access for data, backups, and restricted operations

steps.phase: Track outcomes, audit, and recover
steps.title: Protect rail credentials
steps.content: The dispatcher uses scoped, rotated rail credentials. Signed response verification and least-privilege key access prevent an unauthenticated callback from altering financial status.

connection.label: Rail credentials + verification keys
connection.description: Scoped secret retrieval and callback verification

steps.phase: Track outcomes, audit, and recover
steps.title: Review the unproven operational guarantees
steps.content: Exercise account ownership and verification failures, unauthorized status reads, duplicate requests and concurrent limits, KYC/sanctions review outcomes, model outages, crashes before and after ledger commit, outbox replay, queue redrive, rail timeouts and late callbacks, regional recovery, backup restoration, and audit-archive failure. Verify no acknowledged intent or confirmed outcome disappears and no retry creates a second wire. The brief's zero-tolerance-for-data-loss constraint is a required acceptance goal, not a mathematically proven property of this diagram. The bank must approve jurisdictions, rails, retention, recovery objectives and any quantitative fraud-response target before production use.
